Component guide | Atomization review | Actual saved routes, physical obstacles, and selected cuts
Fixed X/Y tile grid | 1 tile = 16 m | Actual saved DAT/PATH geometry
X (east) — tile centres, 16 m per tile
P01 DD RHW-4 — Straight Diagonal Highway Stamp
P02 RHW Ramp — Lower Full Exit Ramp — R40
P03 RHW Ramp — Lower Full Entry Ramp — R40
P04 RHW Ramp — Upper Full Exit Ramp — R40
P05 RHW Ramp — Upper Full Entry Ramp — R40
P06 RHW Ramp — Northwest Avenue Ramp Terminal — R40
P07 RHW Ramp — Southeast Avenue Ramp Terminal — R40
H: physical mouth. T: city-tile traffic cut.
Grey outlines: indexed pavement, barriers, concrete, and supports.
Dark borders and coloured fills: exclusive tile ownership.
Blue: lower roads. Orange: upper roads.
Grey: ground roads. Green: pedestrian paths.
Retain: straight decks, inside slip lanes, and cutouts.
Move: every curved slab, underside, barrier, and bridge.
Model overhang shares no construction or PATH tile.
Physical mouths: flat at 7.5 m / 15 m; distinct from T cuts.
PATH kinks: lower 1.735 m / upper 3.500 m; new circles R40.
Obstacle: complete Jersey profiles and real supports.
Unverified: universal graded / FLEX building blocks.
H mouths: X, Y tiles; flat pavement height
T traffic cuts: X, Y tiles; actual PATH height
Straight highway stamp: 21 owned tiles. Full R40 attachments: 41. Complete reference: 62 unique construction tiles.
Each lower ramp has 4 traffic ports and 2 intrinsic fragments joined through a stamp-owned middle tile.
The complete visible curved ramps belong to separate pieces; their models deliberately overhang highway-owned tiles.
